authority.local_key_access_control: deviceOwnerAuthentication before Keychain read; Keychain WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly

invariants: The top-level 模型 menu is always visible and never changes Codex model-switch (owned by Ancode) or four-tool credential semantics.

Under 模型 the submenu labels are exactly 状态, 端口, 厂家 and 密钥. Clicking 状态 opens a status panel showing the current Base URL, a provider-scoped call-count line chart (近六小时 / 近一周 / 近一个月) defaulting to the last-used provider, and a control that only opens today's call log file with the system application.

The relay binds only IPv4 loopback 127.0.0.1. It never binds all interfaces, IPv6 wildcard, LAN or a network hostname. Port conflicts leave the relay stopped with an explicit status; no automatic port substitution occurs.
Every route requires a valid generated local Bearer key. Local key authentication uses a constant-time digest comparison and never requires decrypting the copyable secret.

A provider entity has one globally unique display name, one audited OpenAI-compatible preset or validated custom Base URL, and at most one upstream Key. The same preset may be used by multiple entities with different names.

A new or connection-changing provider entity is persisted only after its exact Base URL and candidate Key successfully return a non-empty OpenAI-compatible /models response. Test failure or persistence failure leaves neither provider metadata nor an orphan Keychain item.

Provider create, connection change and delete serialize metadata and Keychain writes. Candidate and retired Key UUIDs are covered by a durable cleanup journal before any crash window; active configuration never references a missing Key, and startup plus periodic refresh retry journal cleanup idempotently.

Provider names, local key names and published model ids are unique in their respective global namespaces. A published model id is derived from the upstream model id (with automatic provider-name prefixing only when needed for uniqueness) and is never user-editable.
Upstream secrets are stored only as generic-password Keychain items using service com.tocode.app.model-relay.upstream and stable UUID accounts. Keychain denial never falls back to plaintext storage.

A generated local key uses at least 32 random bytes and a tc_ prefix. Its copyable secret is stored only as a Keychain generic-password item (service com.tocode.app.model-relay.local, account = key UUID, accessible when unlocked on this device). Metadata persists only the constant-time auth digest (and optional legacy salt/ciphertext until one-time migration). Viewing or deleting requires device-owner authentication (Touch ID or device password) before reading Keychain. HTTP Bearer authentication compares digests only and never requires revealing the copyable secret. Plaintext keys and device passcodes are never persisted outside Keychain.

GET /v1/models returns the enabled published model ids. POST chat/completions and responses replace only the request model id with its upstream model id and otherwise preserve the OpenAI-compatible JSON body.

Each published model id resolves through exactly one provider entity and its single upstream Key. There is no within-entity round-robin or failover; connection errors, 401/403, 429 and 5xx fail explicitly. Once response headers or body/SSE bytes are sent, the request is never retried or spliced.
SSE is forwarded incrementally with backpressure and upstream cancellation when the local client disconnects. Request and response bodies are never logged.

Each inbound POST /v1/chat/completions or /v1/responses counts as exactly one call for observability, including when the upstream session retries or fails. Agent sessions that issue multiple inbound requests are never merged. GET /v1/models is not counted.

Call observability persists only metadata fields ts, route, providerId, providerName, publishedModel, upstreamModel, status, durationMs and ok. Charts aggregate call counts by provider into 10-minute buckets for the last six hours, daily buckets for the last week and weekly buckets for the last month. Token usage is never recorded or displayed.

The day call detail log is a single 0600 file that is truncated and rewritten when the local calendar day changes. Aggregate metrics and lastUsedProviderID are stored separately in a 0600 metrics file retained about 31 days. Neither file may contain Authorization, key material, request bodies or response bodies.
Remote upstream base URLs require HTTPS; HTTP is accepted only for loopback upstreams. Redirects must not leak Authorization to an untrusted host.

Relay providers, published model ids, upstream key references, local keys and device-auth Keychain material never enter .tocode exports, CLI, WeChat commands, keyboard/trackpad mappings, notifications or manual examples. Call metadata logs and aggregate metrics may only live under the approved Application Support paths.
The relay starts and stops with Tocode. The default port is 27800; users may select a fixed port in 1024...65535 and successful changes restart the listener atomically.
prohibited_results: Listening on 0.0.0.0, ::, a LAN interface or any non-loopback endpoint.
Serving models or proxying a request without a valid local Bearer key.
Persisting an upstream key outside Keychain, persisting a local key outside Keychain, or persisting a local/viewing key in plaintext files.
Logging Authorization, key material, request bodies or response bodies.
Recording or displaying token usage as part of relay observability.
Merging multiple inbound POST calls into a single observability record.
Keeping more than one calendar day's call detail log, or writing call logs/metrics without 0600 permissions.
Retrying or changing upstream keys after any response bytes have reached the client.
Treating the relay as an arbitrary HTTP proxy or adding Anthropic/Gemini protocol conversion under this contract.
Exporting relay configuration or secrets through .tocode, CLI, WeChat or mapping features.
Persisting an untested new or changed provider endpoint/Key pair, or retaining more than one Key on a newly written provider entity.
Exposing a user-editable model alias UI or persisting a manually chosen alias that differs from the auto-derived published model id.
Mutating CC Switch or Codex configuration as part of relay CRUD or request routing.
